title: An aggregate-only treatment's interaction is identified by assumption, by an ecological gradient or by the prior, and each fails differently
question: When a treatment has only aggregate data, is its effect-modifier interaction identified by the data, by the shared-interaction assumption, or by the prior, and do credible intervals cover when the assumption fails?
design: Exact conjugate-normal calculation: an individual-data trial for one treatment, one to four aggregate trials for another at spread covariate means, discordance between the two interactions and an ecological term; shared, separate and hierarchical models.
answer: By none of them reliably. With one aggregate trial the data carry no information about the treatment's interaction, yet the shared-interaction model's credible interval was as narrow as the individual-data trial's and covered 0.68 and 0.15 at discordance 0.15 and 0.3; a separate model returned its prior. With four aggregate trials the separate model covered nominally until an ecological term of 0.1 entered the between-trial gradient, then 0.71. The shared model's apparent recovery there came from the ecological bias offsetting the discordance.
findings: Direct share of posterior precision (information about the interaction itself): zero for every model with one aggregate trial.
Shared-model coverage at nonzero discordance without ecological bias: 0.149 to 0.867; separate model with a gradient: 0.942 to 0.955.
With the ecological term, separate-model bias about 0.09 and coverage 0.71 to 0.74.
not_answered: Conjugate normal models on contrast-level data rather than multinma fits; one covariate; fixed prior scales. Peer review has not been done.
estimand: Effect-modifier interaction of the aggregate-only treatment
methods_compared: separate interaction with a vague prior
